title: Schema decorator + runtime coercion and humanized diagnostics for tool calls
creator: Arielle Kim
description: Introduce a JSON-schema ‘decorator’ layer and a runtime coercion/partial-validation path for function/tool calls. Goal: reduce class of user-facing errors without sacrificing deterministic behavior for production workloads. Deliver a compact decorator format (x-*) that augments standard JSON Schema with compatibility and UX hints, implement a permissive-but-visible validation pass that returns structured diagnostics, and expose SDK-friendly error mappings and suggestions. Also add streaming validation for very large payloads and compatibility shims for legacy tool manifests.
acceptance_criteria: Define decorator vocabulary and update model onboarding docs with examples (integers-from-strings, fuzzy-key-match, allow-null-for-optional)

Runtime implements two-phase validation: (1) coercion phase that transforms values according to decorator rules and logs mutations; (2) strict phase that enforces canonical schema and produces diagnostics with severity scores
SDKs return a stable error envelope: error_code, message, field_path, suggestion, diagnostic_score
Canary rollout shows <=5% change in failure-rate for customers using legacy tool manifests and no >1% regression in P95 latency for small calls
Telemetry events for each coercion and top-5 diagnostic reasons are emitted and visible in Console observability dashboards
Security review completed for coercion rules (sanitization, type narrowing) and documented in design notes
technical_decisions: Use JSON Schema Draft-7 as base and reserve x-redwood-* decorator keys for compatibility rules
Provide decorator hints: x-redwood-coerce (number|boolean|date), x-redwood-fuzzy-keys (levenshtein threshold), x-redwood-allow-null, x-redwood-partial-validate (severity thresholds)
Implement coercion as idempotent transformations with an append-only mutation log attached to request trace; disallow coercion for authentication/crypto-related fields
Diagnostics include a numeric diagnostic_score (0-100) encoded as string in envelope to preserve flat JSON; score influences fallback policy (auto-correct vs require user action)
Streaming validators operate on a byte-stream + incremental JSON parser to validate large arrays/files without buffering entire payloads
Backward compatibility: introduce compatibility profiles that map legacy param names to canonical names using x-redwood-compat-aliases; profiles are per-tool and versioned
progress_updates: 2026-03-10 - Kickoff: scoped MVP to coercions for primitive types, fuzzy-key matching, and SDK error envelope. Assigned prototype runtime patch to ENG team.

2026-03-11 - Prototype: Mateo pushed a runtime PoC that applies coercion rules and emits mutation logs. Initial tests for integer-from-string and boolean-from-string pass. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12456
2026-03-12 - PM review: requested additional explicit opt-in guard for x-redwood-coerce on enterprise private deployments. Updated design doc and added security checklist.

2026-03-13 - QA: added unit tests for fuzzy-key matching (threshold edge cases) and streaming validator harness. Found a regression: coercion added for null->default unintentionally; hotfix branch created. Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12478
blockers: Need formal approval from Security for coercion in fields that influence routing/authorization (expected decision by 2026-03-16)
Compatibility profile storage design: whether to store per-customer profiles in central control plane or bundle with tool manifest (affects privacy and latency)
SDK mapping for older SDKs lacking structured error envelopes requires cross-team coordination with SDK owners
open_questions: Should coercion be opt-in per-organization by default or opt-out? (PM prefers opt-in)
What is the acceptable mutation log retention time for privacy-sensitive customers?
How should we surface multi-field validation issues (e.g., dependent fields) in the diagnostic_score model?
qa_plan: Unit tests for coercion rules and mutation log correctness
Fuzz tests for fuzzy-key matcher (randomized key sets and thresholds)
Integration test with SDK: ensure error envelope round-trips across JS/Python runtimes
Performance benchmark: compare P50/P95 latency with and without streaming validation on 1KB, 100KB, and 10MB payloads
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): Enable for internal accounts and 5% of hosted API traffic; monitor telemetry for failure-rate deltas
Phase 2 (Beta): Offer as opt-in feature flag in Console; gather customer feedback and adjust fuzzy thresholds
Phase 3 (GA): Default behavior for new tool manifests; existing manifests remain opt-out unless customer upgrades their manifest version
notes_from_reviewers: PM Dana Holt: 'Strong +1 for structured suggestions in SDK errors, but require clear opt-in for coercion in sensitive contexts.'
Design Lea Park: 'Please include example UX in Console showing before/after for common errors (missing trailing slash, number vs string). UI will need mapping from diagnostic_score to color scale.'
Security Omar Singh: 'We need a formal threat model for coerced values—especially anything that could change routing or SQL-like filters. Blocked until we get quick review.'
